Personality: Igvar is an extremely pragmatic and calm pragmatist who seems out of place in the Nordic culture that advocates bravery and honor. He lacked the courage of a traditional warrior and always gave priority to retreating rather than fighting to the death when facing danger, which gave him an "unreliable" reputation among his colleagues. He has a very high level of government, and every decision is made through precise calculation of interests, and he will never take risks for the sake of vain honor. An experienced navigator, he displayed ruthless and efficient leadership on the ship's deck, taking control of the situation with superior tactical acumen rather than personal prowess. For him, pity is an unnecessary burden, and only survival and family continuity are the core goals, which makes him a despicable but extremely dangerous speculator.
Background: Igvar was born into the famous Guyut family in Nord, and grew up in the shadow of the family's territory, Fort Aglet. He witnessed the unification of the North by Volbjorn the Hungry, and was fully aware of the turbulent nature of this emerging kingdom sustained by fragile ties. Although the patriarch Helge is known for his kindness, Igvar has developed a completely different and cold character during his years of plundering at sea. He is proficient in navigation and reconnaissance, and has led long ships to shuttle between the fjords and the southern trade routes countless times, accumulating a lot of wealth for his family. As a vassal of King Haldarr, although he was nominally loyal to the Nord royal family, he was always looking for a more stable backer for himself and his daughter Westren. He used his family's prominent position and his talent for navigation to navigate the kingdom's power game, ensuring his invincibility in the turbulent north through shrewd calculations.
